<a name="Service"></a>
## type [Service](<https://github.com/takoterm/tako/blob/main/internal/ui/dialog/service.go#L27-L32>)

Service implements \[contracts.DialogService\].

It is UI\-agnostic: it never renders anything itself. Instead it:

1. Registers the message text as a hook provider under "tako.overlay.tako.dialog.confirm" so the developer's layout can display it.
2. Pushes the overlay via the OverlayManager.
3. Registers ephemeral key bindings at the dialog's stack level.

The bindings are registered at the specific stack level the dialog occupies, so they are naturally scoped — they stop firing once the layer is popped, without requiring explicit cleanup.

Service is obtained via app.Overlay\(\).Dialog\(\) or ctx.Overlay\(\).Dialog\(\). It is not meant to be constructed or held directly by host\-app code.

```go [service.go]
    // contains filtered or unexported fields

```

<a name="New"></a>
### func [New](<https://github.com/takoterm/tako/blob/main/internal/ui/dialog/service.go#L37>)

```go [service.go]
func New(r *router.Router, bus contracts.EventBus) *Service
```

New creates a new Service. The OverlayManager is not set at construction time to break the initialization cycle between overlay.Manager and dialog.Service — call SetOverlayManager immediately after both are created.

<a name="Service.Confirm"></a>
### func \(\*Service\) [Confirm](<https://github.com/takoterm/tako/blob/main/internal/ui/dialog/service.go#L70>)

```go [service.go]
func (s *Service) Confirm(message string, onResult func(yes bool))
```

Confirm pushes a confirmation dialog overlay. When the user presses y/enter \(accept\) or n/esc \(cancel\), onResult is called with the appropriate boolean, the overlay is dismissed, and an event is emitted on the EventBus.

The message is exposed as the render output of the "tako.overlay.tako.dialog.confirm" hook so the developer's layout can style and display it however they wish.

Events emitted:

- "dialog:confirmed" — user pressed y or enter
- "dialog:cancelled" — user pressed n or esc

Usage \(via OverlayManager\):

```
app.Overlay().Dialog().Confirm("Delete this file?", func(yes bool) {
    if yes { doDelete() }
})
```

<a name="Service.SetOverlayManager"></a>
### func \(\*Service\) [SetOverlayManager](<https://github.com/takoterm/tako/blob/main/internal/ui/dialog/service.go#L47>)

```go [service.go]
func (s *Service) SetOverlayManager(o contracts.OverlayManager)
```

SetOverlayManager wires the OverlayManager into the Service. This must be called before any dialog method is invoked. It is called automatically by overlay.Manager during its own construction.
